title: المرَكَباتُ وَالجُمَلُ – Sentences and Phrases
summary: This section introduces the basics of Arabic sentences and phrases, focusing on complete and incomplete sentences, nominal and verbal sentences, and various types of inshaiyyah sentences.

revision_notes.heading: Complete vs. Incomplete Sentences
revision_notes.explanation: In Arabic, sentences can be complete (كلام تَام) or incomplete (كلام نَاقِص). Complete sentences are self-sufficient, while incomplete sentences lack some elements.

revision_notes.heading: Nominal Sentence (جُمْلَة إِسْمِيَّة)
revision_notes.explanation: A nominal sentence starts with a noun (المُبْتَدَأ) followed by a predicate (الخَبَر). Both parts are usually in the nominative case (مَرْفُوعَة).

revision_notes.heading: Verbal Sentence (جُمْلَةٌ فِعْلِيَّةٌ)
revision_notes.explanation: A verbal sentence starts with a verb (الفِعْلُ), followed by the subject (الفَاعِلُ) which is always in the nominative case (مَرْفُوعٌ).

revision_notes.heading: Types of Inshaiyyah Sentences
revision_notes.explanation: There are ten types of inshaiyyah sentences including commands, interrogatives, exclamations, etc., each serving a specific communicative function.

flashcards.back: A complete sentence that is self-sufficient.

flashcards.front: What is المُبْتَدَأ in a جُمْلَة إِسْمِيَّة?
flashcards.back: The subject or the word about which information is given.

flashcards.front: What is the خَبَر in a جُمْلَة إِسْمِيَّة?
flashcards.back: The predicate or the word giving the information.

key_terms.simple_explanation: A sentence that is self-sufficient and does not require additional information.
A sentence that lacks some elements and is not self-sufficient.
A sentence that starts with a noun.

quiz.question: Which part of a جُمْلَة إِسْمِيَّة is called المُبْتَدَأ?
quiz.explanation: The المُبْتَدَأ is the subject or the word about which information is given.

quiz.question: In a جُمْلَةٌ فِعْلِيَّةٌ, the subject (الفَاعِلُ) is always in the accusative case.
quiz.explanation: The subject (الفَاعِلُ) in a جُمْلَةٌ فِعْلِيَّةٌ is always in the nominative case (مَرْفُوعٌ).

quiz.question: The first part of a جُمْلَة إِسْمِيَّة is called ________.
quiz.explanation: The first part of a جُمْلَة إِسْمِيَّة is called المُبْتَدَأ, which means the subject.

exercise_answers.question: المعلم حاضر
exercise_answers.reason: It is a جُمْلَة إِسْمِيَّة where المعلم is the subject and حاضر is the predicate.

exercise_answers.question: البستان جميل
exercise_answers.reason: It is a جُمْلَة إِسْمِيَّة where البستان is the subject and جميل is the predicate.

exercise_answers.question: فتح محمد الباب
exercise_answers.reason: It is a جُمْلَةٌ فِعْلِيَّةٌ where فتح is the verb, محمد is the subject, and الباب is the object.

exercise_answers.question: المدرسة كبيرة نظيفة
exercise_answers.reason: It is a جُمْلَة إِسْمِيَّة where المدرسة is the subject and كبيرة نظيفة are the predicates.

exercise_answers.question: وقف الرجل
exercise_answers.reason: It is a جُمْلَةٌ فِعْلِيَّةٌ where وقف is the verb and الرجل is the subject.

exercise_answers.question: الرجل وقف
exercise_answers.reason: It is also a جُمْلَةٌ فِعْلِيَّةٌ but with the verb and subject inverted.

exercise_answers.question: What is the difference between (v) and (vi)?
exercise_answers.answer: The order of the verb and subject is different.
exercise_answers.reason: In (v), the verb comes before the subject, while in (vi), the subject comes before the verb, but both convey the same meaning.
